title: BP Signs Offshore Natural Gas Exploration Pact with Venezuela
detail: British Petroleum (BP) and Venezuela's transitional government signed a major offshore natural gas exploration agreement at the Miraflores Palace in Caracas on April 29, 2026. Acting President Delcy Rodríguez declared 'This is the return of BP to Venezuela' during the signing ceremony. The deal represents one of the most significant international energy investments in Venezuela since comprehensive US sanctions were imposed in 2017–2019. The agreement signals growing confidence among Western energy majors that Venezuela's post-Maduro transition government is stable enough for long-term investment. Venezuela holds the world's largest certified proven oil reserves and significant untapped natural gas reserves in the Caribbean offshore zone. BP had previously had operations in Venezuela before withdrawing under the Chávez nationalisation wave.

media.caption: BP and Venezuela sign offshore natural gas exploration agreement at Miraflores Palace

title: Guyana Formally Protests Delcy Rodríguez Essequibo Brooch During Caribbean Visits
detail: Guyana's President Irfaan Ali formally protested Venezuela's Acting President Delcy Rodríguez for wearing a gold brooch depicting Venezuela's map inclusive of the Essequibo region — the 160,000 km² oil-rich territory administered by Guyana but claimed by Venezuela — during official visits to Grenada (April 9) and Barbados (April 27–28). Ali denounced what he called the 'ostentatious exhibition of symbols' asserting territorial claims over sovereign Guyanese territory. The diplomatic incident came just days before the International Court of Justice (ICJ) was set to begin oral hearings on the Guyana–Venezuela border dispute on May 4. The Essequibo is central to Venezuela's national identity and its claim is backed by all Venezuelan political factions including the transitional government.

media.caption: Delcy Rodríguez's Essequibo brooch triggers formal Guyana diplomatic protest
